What makes Professor Olsen incredibly unique as a teacher is his masterful grasp of the teaching material. Unlike many of his colleagues  who simply give a general and superficial explanation of literary periods or movements, his lessons make for holistic experiences, delving into a plethora of subjects, from history to philosophy, from religion to the politics. The only things that limit him in a sense are the duration of the courses and the vastness of his knowledge (in that he has to inevitably choose what to go over). Moreover,  his sophisticated sense of humour provides immense accessibility to his lectures, adding a certain levity to otherwise heavy topics. From a more personal perspective, his impeccable fashion sense and kindly smile make him a very endearing personality. One does not feel alienated or looked down on when in his presence, which is what many teachers attempt and fail to foster in their pupils. Overall, my only gripe with Professor Olsen is his tendency to go on vacations every now and then, which obviously results in the cancellation of his courses.
